subject: Post-call: eval roadmap & hyperscaler gap analysis for embeddings + rerank
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire@searchly.ai>, Marcus Dean <m.dean@arcussearch.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-02T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + prioritized eval plan

Thanks again for your time today — good convo and great signal on where ArcusSearch is trying to get on ranking quality without blowing up cost. Quick recap and a proposed evaluation roadmap so we can move to a short A/B test next week.

Call recap (very short):
- Primary ask: improve search relevance for long-tail queries and knowledge-heavy documents; current baseline is Vertex-hosted embeddings + a simple cosine reranker.
- Constraints: 99ms p95 retrieval budget for web UI, throughput ~80 qps peak, storage/cost sensitivity (want to estimate $/million vectors).
- Success metrics you care about: recall@1/5/10, MRR, end-to-end median latency, and cost per 10k queries.

What Redwood proposes (high level differentiators):
1) Embedding quality: model choices with tuned dims (1024 vs 1536) and quant-friendly outputs to reduce storage/cost.
2) Retrieval latency controls: autoscaled ANN + warmed caches and prefix caching to hit p95 SLOs with lower CPU/GPU cost.
3) Rerank stack: light candidate-generator + dedicated low-latency reranker (opt for >50ms p95 on small models) vs sending everything to a large cross-attention model.
4) Cost transparency: token + vector storage + ANN index cost breakdown per workload so you can estimate unit economics.

Proposed prioritized test matrix (short run to unblock procurement):
- Dataset: start with your 10k sample queries + 100k doc corpus (use the CSV you shared).
- Baselines to run in parallel (3 lanes):
  A) Current: Vertex embeddings (dim 1536) + cosine + Vertex reranker (as you have today).
  B) Redwood-hosted embeddings (gpt-embed-2-small, dim 1024) + FAISS HNSW CPU index + Redwood rerank (redwood-rerank-lite).
  C) Redwood-hosted quantized embeddings (1024 -> 8-bit PQ) + hybrid IVF_PQ + GPU FAISS + Redwood low-latency rerank.
- Metrics to capture per-query: recall@1/5/10, MRR, raw ANN recall, retrieval p50/p95, rerank p50/p95, end-to-end p50/p95, cost estimate ($/10k queries).
- Approx sizes: index memory for 100k docs (expected ~500MB for 1024 dim 8-bit PQ) — we'll measure precisely.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Claire/Marcus: share the sample-query-set.csv and a small doc export (100k docs). You mentioned a shared Drive link — if you post that we can start. (Attachment: sample-query-set.csv)
2) Redwood (Dylan): spin up three lanes and return an initial recall/latency table by EOD 6/4.
3) Soojin/Marissa: prepare a cost sheet (tokens + vector storage + index compute) to review on the next call.

Attachments: call-recording-20260602.mp3 (recording), sample-query-set.csv (your sample).

Open questions we flagged:
- Does Arcus want quantization artifacts to be prioritized (some customers prefer exact float at small cost premium)?
- Any legal or procurement gating for a short evaluation cluster (we can run everything on hosted Redwood tenancy if preferred).

If that matches your readout, I’ll kick off the lanes and we’ll sync after the initial run.

—
Soojin Lee
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-06-02T17:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + prioritized eval plan

Thanks, Soojin — this is great and aligns with what we want. I uploaded the initial artifacts to the Drive folder and attached the sample query CSV to this reply.

Quick notes:
- We prefer to preserve float embeddings for our canonical index but are open to testing 8-bit PQ if the drop in relevance is negligible — please surface accuracy vs storage tradeoffs in the report.
- Procurement: I can sign an MSA addendum for an evaluation if needed; Marcus is handling approvals but expects a short eval PO.

I’ve attached: sample-query-set.csv (same as in Drive), and a light export of 100k docs as docs-100k-lite.jsonl (link in Drive).

Would it be possible to get the first run of the recall table by COB Friday (6/4)? That will allow Marcus to include a conservative estimate in the PO.

Thanks — Claire
Claire Huang
Head of Product, ArcusSearch
claire@searchly.ai
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Claire Huang <claire@searchly.ai>, Marcus Dean <m.dean@arcussearch.com>
Date: 2026-06-03T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Post-call recap + prioritized eval plan — action items for Redwood

Dylan / Marissa — forwarding Claire's confirmation and the Drive links. Summary of your action items (please add ETA inline):
1) Dylan: stand up three test lanes described in the matrix (A/B/C). Use the provided 100k docs + 10k queries. Capture recall@1/5/10, MRR, ANN recall, retrieval p50/p95, rerank p50/p95, and compute an estimated cost per 10k queries. Put initial results in Drive under rd-2247/results/initial.csv. ETA: please aim for 6/4 COB.
2) Marissa: produce a short cost breakdown comparing Vertex baseline vs Redwood lanes (vector storage, index compute, rerank token cost). Include a few scenario lines: 10k qps-month, 1M vectors. ETA: 6/4 EOD.
3) Both: document index configs (HNSW params, PQ bytes per vector) and ANN run parameters so Arcus can reproduce.

A couple implementation notes that came up on the call:
- For fairness, set Vertex baseline to their standard 1536-dim model and measure raw cosine recall.
- Run each lane with 3 repeated runs and take medians for latency.

If you see blockers (quota, Drive access), flag me and I’ll escalate.

—
Soojin
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Claire Huang <claire@searchly.ai>
Date: 2026-06-05T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + prioritized eval plan — initial run status

Quick status update — initial runs are executing now in Redwood hosted lanes. Early observations (preliminary):
- Lane B (1024, HNSW CPU) recall@10 is already within ~2% of Vertex baseline on a small subset (1k queries); retrieval p95 ~82ms (we can tune HNSW efConstruction/efSearch to push p95 lower).
- Lane C (8-bit PQ + GPU FAISS) shows retrieval p50 ~18ms but we need to verify recall delta at top1 — running the full 10k query sweep now.
- We saw an unexpected artifact with one document shard where vector normalization differed (fixing normalization will be in the run script).

Deliverables ETA: full recall/latency table in Drive and the initial-benchmark-results.pdf by EOD 6/05 (will include cost estimates and index configs).

Attachments to come: initial-benchmark-results.pdf (summary), run-configs.json (index params).

—
Dylan Brooks
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
